core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 880-884): the kernel of f represents the functor sending z to the kernel of the induced map between the Hom-sets, so it vanishes exactly when that map is injective for every z, which is the definition of a monomorphism.
Part (2) (proof line 885): the corresponding statement for epimorphisms is proved in the same way.

Part (3) (proof lines 886-891): an isomorphism is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism, so by (1) and (2) it is injective and surjective; conversely, if f is injective and surjective then the source is the coimage of f and the target is its image, whence f is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Translate the vanishing of the kernel into injectivity of the induced maps on Hom-sets.
Combine the two for the characterization of isomorphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies injective, surjective and bijective morphisms of an abelian category with monomorphisms, epimorphisms and isomorphisms (statement lines 869-877). The proof is a complete argument: the first equivalence is obtained by writing the kernel as the object representing the functor of kernels of the induced maps on Hom-sets (proof lines 880-884); the second is the same argument (proof line 885); and the third combines the first two with the identification of the source with the coimage and the target with the image of a morphism that is both injective and surjective (proof lines 886-891). The non-formal content is the representability translation. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
